quorum.kill_rule: majority of three judges; CONFIRMED-AS-NARROWED counts as survived, because every narrowing moved a citation anchor and kept the substance
refuted_claims: The live test properly manages four combinations of sudo presence and FORJAR_REQUIRE_SUDO_TESTS — REFUTED: the variable is set in no workflow, Makefile or config, so the fail-closed branch never engages in CI and tests/falsification_sudo_transport_survives_closefrom.rs skips wherever passwordless sudo is absent; the emulated test is the sole runtime falsifier.

The strictness test's ordered byte-offset checks still risk passing vacuously — REFUTED by J2 and J3 on contradictory readings, resolved by reading the file at both ends: at base tests/falsification_390e_nested_shell_strictness.rs:150 is the message of a plain script.contains("sudo bash /dev/fd/3 3<<'") assertion, so J3's "no offset logic" describes the base file; at HEAD the test asserts mktemp < trap && trap < cat and requires `sudo bash "$forjar_sudo_script"` after the heredoc's closing delimiter, so the offsets exist and are what removes the vacuity the claim says remains.
quorum.divergence: Two of the three judges returned do-not-implement-as-written, and neither verdict is about the fix: both scored 'does the fix close the defect' 5 of 5 and objected to CLAIM TEXT — imprecise citations and two unsupported test claims. Refuter R1's most aggressive attack was itself fabricated (it asserted tests_sudo.rs spawns bash through a run_as_transport helper; J2 and J3 independently read the file and found only .contains()).

crux.verdict: forjar's temp-file transport matches Ansible and Terraform in the property that matters: the script crosses the privilege boundary as a FILE ARGUMENT, which is exactly what makes it immune to sudo's closefrom, while SaltStack and Puppet avoid the transition entirely by running a long-lived root agent. R3's four hardening gaps — attacker-controlled TMPDIR, no explicit umask, no sticky-bit check, no cleanup on SIGKILL — were ruled NON-BLOCKING by all three judges, and for a stated reason: the comparators execute remotely as a different principal, whereas this wrapper is generated for the invoking user's own local shell, mktemp opens with O_EXCL at 0600, and SIGKILL is uncatchable by POSIX design in every one of the four systems too.
crux.source: refuter-3 carried both the crux survey and the R3 attack; the lane briefed as crux returned one claim and no survey, which is recorded as a lane shortfall in .quorum/evidence/sudo-fd3-lanes.md rather than re-labelled

agy_teamwork.verdict: The file transport fix is robust. It uses mktemp safely, isolates stdin as intended, handles disk-full scenarios gracefully, and preserves the exact exit status (even on signals like ^C) because the cleanup traps do not call exit. The new emulated-closefrom test correctly falsifies the old broken behavior.
unique_findings: stated the exit-status argument as a mechanism rather than an assertion: the status survives because a bash EXIT trap that does not itself call exit leaves the last command's status in place, which is why the wrapper needs no explicit save-and-restore

was the only review to ask what happens when the transport half FAILS — mktemp and cat are each guarded with || exit 1, so an invalid TMPDIR or a full disk stops the wrapper before it elevates anything
agy_teamwork.did_not_cover: it ran no field survey, and it did not examine whether the live-privilege test can ever run in CI — the finding that killed claim B3

RESOLUTION of refuted claim 1 (the live test skipped in CI because FORJAR_REQUIRE_SUDO_TESTS was set nowhere): .github/workflows/ci.yml examples-validate now carries a second step, "The sudo transport survives closefrom under real sudo (required, not skippable)", with env FORJAR_REQUIRE_SUDO_TESTS: "1" running `cargo test --locked --test falsification_sudo_transport_survives_closefrom`. With the variable set, a missing capability panics in missing() at tests/falsification_sudo_transport_survives_closefrom.rs:64 instead of printing SKIP, so a green step means the gated tests EXECUTED under real sudo, not that they declined to. The job runs on ubuntu-latest, where the `runner` user is non-root with passwordless sudo by GitHub's documented hosted-runner environment — cited, not measured here, and if it ever stops holding this step fails loudly rather than silently skipping. Measured on lambda-labs 2026-09-05 (uid 1000, passwordless sudo): the same command exits 0 with `6 passed; 0 failed` and no SKIP line; the negative, the same command with a PATH whose `sudo` exits 1, exits 101 with 5 of 6 tests panicking "FORJAR_REQUIRE_SUDO_TESTS=1 but <test> cannot run: `sudo -n true` fails on this host". The claim lanes did not see this step; a D1 review of it is to follow, as for the emulated step above.

RESOLUTION of refuted claim 2 (the strictness test's ordered byte-offset checks): resolved by reading the file at both ends, not by changing code. At base, `git show origin/main:tests/falsification_390e_nested_shell_strictness.rs` line 150 is the MESSAGE STRING of a plain `script.contains("sudo bash /dev/fd/3 3<<'")` assertion spanning lines 148-151 — there is no offset logic there, which is the file J3 was describing. At HEAD the same test, the_sudo_wrapper_is_stdin_isolated_and_collision_free, resolves byte offsets with a `find` closure at tests/falsification_390e_nested_shell_strictness.rs:157-161, takes mktemp@162, trap@163 and cat@164, and asserts `mktemp < trap && trap < cat` at :165-169; it then parses the heredoc delimiter out of the script at :174-178, locates the closing delimiter at :179-183, and asserts `sudo bash "$forjar_sudo_script"` (at :184) occurs AFTER that close at :185-190. The ordered offsets the claim says are missing are therefore present at HEAD and are exactly what removes the vacuity two disconnected `contains` calls would leave. No further change is warranted.
